scenes.tts: Why does a fragment bring back a whole memory? A few notes of a song, and the rest returns.
scenes.visual: Title fades. A few musical notes and a small corner of a room drift in; faint outlines of the full song sheet and the full room fill in around them. On screen: Why does a part recall the whole?
scenes.narration: Why does a fragment bring back a whole memory? A few notes of a song, and the rest returns.

scenes.tts: A rat runs a track while one hippocampal cell is recorded. Each spike drops a dot where the rat was.
scenes.visual: Overhead camera view of a rat on a long track, a small hippocampus inset with an electrode in the corner. The path draws as a grey line; red dots drop wherever the cell spikes and cluster in one stretch.
scenes.narration: A rat runs a track while one hippocampal cell is recorded. Each spike drops a dot where the rat was.

scenes.tts: Divide the floor into bins, and divide each bin's spikes by the time spent there.
scenes.visual: A grid of bins overlays the floor. One bin highlights with two labels: spikes, and seconds spent. On screen: rate = spikes / time spent.
scenes.narration: Divide the floor into bins, and divide each bin's spikes by the time spent there.

scenes.tts: One hot spot is a place field, and this is a place cell.
scenes.visual: Bins colour by rate from dark blue to bright yellow. One yellow hot spot glows, labelled place field. Colour bar: spikes per second.
scenes.narration: One hot spot is a place field, and this is a place cell.

scenes.tts: Each place cell fires in its own stretch, so a run is a sequence of cells.
scenes.visual: Five place cells drawn as circles above the track, each with its own coloured field. As the rat runs, the circles light in order, left to right.
scenes.narration: Each place cell fires in its own stretch, so a run is a sequence of cells.

scenes.tts: One run engages a set of cells, firing in order.
scenes.visual: The five lit circles keep their firing order, and a soft outline encloses them. Label: one run, one set of cells, fired in order. A faint second outline overlaps part of it, labelled sets can overlap.
scenes.narration: One run engages a set of cells, firing in order.

scenes.tts: Now store a pattern in four model units. Agreeing units get a positive link, disagreeing units a negative one.
scenes.visual: Four units in a square, labelled 1 to 4, states plus, plus, minus, minus. Thick green links join units 1 and 2, and 3 and 4; dashed red links join each plus unit to each minus unit. Corner label: teaching model, not hippocampal measurements.
scenes.narration: Now store a pattern in four model units. Agreeing units get a positive link, disagreeing units a negative one.

scenes.tts: Start from a cue with unit one wrong.
scenes.visual: Unit 1 turns from plus to minus and is outlined in orange. On screen: cue (minus, plus, minus, minus).
scenes.narration: Start from a cue with unit one wrong.

scenes.tts: Each partner sends it a vote: link times state. Which way will unit one go?
scenes.visual: Three arrows travel from units 2, 3 and 4 to unit 1, each tagged link times state, signs hidden behind question marks. On screen: Which way does unit 1 go?
scenes.narration: Each partner sends it a vote: link times state. Which way will unit one go?

scenes.tts: All three votes say plus. Unit one flips, and the stored pattern is back.
scenes.visual: The arrow tags reveal plus, plus, plus. On screen: field = +3/4. Unit 1 flips to plus; the square reads plus, plus, minus, minus, with a check mark: stored pattern.
scenes.narration: All three votes say plus. Unit one flips, and the stored pattern is back.

scenes.tts: The energy counts violated links. The cue violates three, and the stored pattern none.
scenes.visual: Back to the cue: the three links to unit 1 flash red with a cross; the other three stay green. On screen: 3 violated, energy 0. Then the stored pattern: none violated, energy -1.5.
scenes.narration: The energy counts violated links. The cue violates three, and the stored pattern none.

scenes.tts: Each flip removes more violation than it adds, so the state rolls downhill into a valley.
scenes.visual: The square shrinks into a ball on an energy landscape that rolls into a deep valley labelled stored pattern; across a ridge, a second valley is labelled inverse (minus, minus, plus, plus), a quirk of this model.
scenes.narration: Each flip removes more violation than it adds, so the state rolls downhill into a valley.

scenes.tts: So here is the idea. Learning strengthens links among cells active together.
scenes.visual: The square fades back into the cluster of place cells; the links between them thicken. On screen: Learning strengthens links among cells active together.
scenes.narration: So here is the idea. Learning strengthens links among cells active together.

scenes.tts: Later, a fragment close enough to the stored pattern pulls the rest back on.
scenes.visual: Two cells of the cluster light; the light spreads along the thick links until the whole cluster glows. On screen: a close-enough fragment pulls the rest back on.
scenes.narration: Later, a fragment close enough to the stored pattern pulls the rest back on.

scenes.tts: In this model, recall is the group completing itself.
scenes.visual: Full cluster lit. On screen, large: In the model, recall = the group completing itself.
scenes.narration: In this model, recall is the group completing itself.

scenes.tts: The hippocampal region C A three has dense recurrent connections, so it is modelled this way.
scenes.caption: The hippocampal region CA3 has dense recurrent connections, so it is modelled this way.
scenes.visual: Schematic hippocampus with CA3 highlighted; looping arrows show recurrent connections between its pyramidal cells. Label: CA3, modelled as an attractor network.
scenes.narration: The hippocampal region CA3 has dense recurrent connections, so it is modelled this way.

scenes.tts: The idea has limits. C A three's pyramidal-cell connections are excitatory, and in the brain, inhibition helps regulate how many cells join in.
scenes.visual: Many overlapping groups of cells, all links drawn as green excitatory arrows, a single dial labelled fixed threshold. Corner label: some models, many stored groups.
scenes.narration: The idea has limits. C A three's pyramidal-cell connections are excitatory, and in the brain, inhibition helps regulate how many cells join in.

scenes.tts: In some models, a low threshold lets activity spread into other groups, and a high one leaves a weak cue unable to recruit its own.
scenes.visual: Split screen, both panels labelled possible failure mode, some models. Left, threshold low: a small fragment lights its group, then activity spreads into other groups. Right, threshold high: a weak fragment fades without recruiting its group.
scenes.narration: In some models, a low threshold lets activity spread into other groups, and a high one leaves a weak cue unable to recruit its own.

scenes.tts: Feedback inhibition that tracks the total can keep activity sparse. With suitable connections and a good enough cue, a fragment can then complete its own pattern.
scenes.visual: A dimmer dial labelled inhibition rises as more cells light; from a small lit fragment, the network settles with only the stored group lit. Label: one possible retrieval, model network.
scenes.narration: Feedback inhibition that tracks the total can keep activity sparse. With suitable connections and a good enough cue, a fragment can then complete its own pattern.

scenes.tts: Storing more patterns reshapes the landscape. Basins shrink, and false valleys appear. A poor cue can roll into the wrong one.
scenes.visual: As more patterns are stored, the landscape changes: some valleys grow shallower or vanish, and new shallow valleys appear, labelled spurious mixture. A ball labelled poor cue rolls into a wrong valley; a ball labelled good cue still reaches the right one.
scenes.narration: Storing more patterns reshapes the landscape. Basins shrink, and false valleys appear. A poor cue can roll into the wrong one.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking N M D A receptors only in C A three pyramidal cells learned a water maze normally.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking NMDA receptors only in CA3 pyramidal cells learned a water maze normally.
scenes.visual: A circular water maze with a hidden platform and four room cues on the walls. A mouse swims to the platform. Label: NMDA receptors deleted in CA3 pyramidal cells only.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking NMDA receptors only in CA3 pyramidal cells learned a water maze normally.

scenes.tts: With all the room cues they recalled the platform. With few cues, they searched poorly.
scenes.visual: Two panels. Left: all four cues, the search path tight around the platform location. Right: most cues removed, the path wanders widely. Labels: all cues, normal; few cues, impaired.
scenes.narration: With all the room cues they recalled the platform. With few cues, they searched poorly.

scenes.tts: That is the deficit the model predicts. But completion was inferred from behaviour, not recorded in C A three.
scenes.caption: That is the deficit the model predicts. But completion was inferred from behaviour, not recorded in CA3.
scenes.visual: The two panels shrink beside the energy landscape. On screen: consistent with completion in CA3; inferred, not recorded there.
scenes.narration: That is the deficit the model predicts. But completion was inferred from behaviour, not recorded in CA3.

scenes.tts: In this model, recall is a group of linked cells completing itself from a part.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: A close-enough cue can recall the whole, if the network is not too full.
scenes.narration: In this model, recall is a group of linked cells completing itself from a part.
